candidate.blueprint_topic: Management of Care — role transition, supervision, coaching and professional support
candidate.educational_objective: Differentiate the preceptor role from mentorship by recognizing the preceptor’s structured role in clinical transition, coaching, evaluation, and feedback.

options.A: A long-term career adviser who supports professional development but does not participate in clinical orientation or competency feedback.
options.B: An experienced, competent nurse who serves as a role model and resource, coaches the new nurse into the role, evaluates performance, and provides feedback for improvement.
options.C: A disciplinary manager whose primary function is enforcing attendance and employment rules rather than coaching transition into the clinical role.
options.D: A peer selected only for social support who does not observe clinical practice, evaluate performance, or provide role-specific feedback.

candidate.rationale: Open RN describes preceptors as experienced and competent nurses who serve as role models and resources to newly hired nurses, coach them into the nursing role, answer questions, evaluate performance, and provide feedback for improvement. B directly matches this description.
candidate.source_claim_supported: A nursing preceptor is an experienced competent nurse who supports transition into practice through role modeling, coaching, performance evaluation, and feedback.
